subject: Clarify data custody, retention scope & evidence for SIG questionnaire
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@megabank.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@megabank.com>; legal@megabank.com
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: custody / retention / encryption scope

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the SIG intake this morning. Procurement had a few clarification asks from our InfoSec and Legal teams so we can close scope for the RFP:

1) Data custody: For requests routed to Redwood Hosted, can you confirm whether customer PII or transaction blobs are retained on your hosted nodes beyond request processing? If retained, what's the retention window and physical location (region) of that data?

2) Backups & snapshots: Do backups of model-serving instances include request payloads or logs that contain PII? If so, please describe the retention and controls.

3) Encryption & key custody: Who holds KMS keys for hosted deployments? Are there customer-owned KMS options?

4) Evidence needs: Our auditor wants a short list of artifacts we can expect to receive to substantiate your answers (examples: retention policy excerpt, dataflow diagram, SOC 2 evidence list). Can you provide an approximate delivery ETA?

We'd like to lock scope by EOD tomorrow so legal can incorporate it into the contract. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if easier.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Sr. Procure Manager — Mega Bank

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@megabank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: custody / retention / encryption scope

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and we can attach the artifacts you requested by EOD Monday: 

1) Data custody (hosted): We do not persist customer input/output beyond the completion of the inference call by default. Temporary request buffers and KV cache entries live in-memory on serving nodes and are cleared after the session TTL. For customers who enable Redwoods' optional request-logging, those logs are stored with encryption at rest; default retention is 30 days but configurable via contract. Hosted data centers: primary US regions (us-west-2, us-east-1).

2) Backups & snapshots: Infrastructure-level snapshots (for OS and model artifacts) do not include customer request payloads. Application logs that contain identifiers are separated and only included in backups when request-logging is enabled by the customer; those backups are retained per the configured retention policy (default 30 days).

3) Encryption & keys: For hosted, Redwood manages KMS keys by default (AWS KMS in-region). We offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments and an option for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for Hosted via a negotiated contract.

4) Evidence & ETA: We'll provide the following artifacts Monday EOD: a one-page retention_policy_snippet.pdf, the service dataflow_diagram_v3.png, SOC2 artifact index (redwood_soc2_artifact_list.xlsx), and an access_matrix.csv showing role-level access. I'll copy Legal on any items that require redlines.

If that works, I'll also propose a 30-min call Monday to walk the auditor through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Compliance & GTM Risk
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: evidence prep + redlines to expected artifacts

Lauren / Rishi —

Following Samantha's ask, I'm drafting the artifact packet. A couple of quick internal notes / asks before we send: 

- retention_policy_snippet.pdf: make sure we include the paragraph that explicitly states default 30-day request-log retention and the opt-out/extend options.
- dataflow_diagram_v3.png: use anonymized flow (no customer IDs), but show where KV cache and ephemeral storage sit and the TTL.
- redwood_soc2_artifact_list.xlsx: include SOC 2 control IDs that map to SIG sections (e.g., CC4.1, CC6.2) to speed auditor mapping.
- access_matrix.csv: we need to flag who has production key access. Can we include the list of custodian roles but redact user-level names?

Also there's a legal ask: Mega's procurement asked about retention for archived evaluation datasets (customer-provided prompts used for fine-tuning/evals). We currently mark eval datasets as "customer-owned" and recommend Private/Dedicated for long-term storage. Rishi, can you confirm the exact wording we should provide?

I'll assemble the packet and drop a shared Drive link.

—Kim

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: evidence prep + redlines to expected artifacts

Kim / Lauren —

On evaluation datasets: confirm the guidance below when responding to Mega Bank and Legal: 

- Evaluation datasets provided by customers for model quality testing are treated as customer data. By default we do not persist those datasets in Hosted beyond the evaluation job lifecycle. If a customer requests long-term retention for continuous evals / fine-tuning, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment with explicit contract terms that cover storage, access controls, and key custody.

- For Hosted customers who opt into the evaluation storage feature, data is stored in an isolated bucket with encryption at rest; retention is configurable and subject to contractual SLAs.

I'll add a short sentence to the retention_policy_snippet to capture this. Also attaching a proposed redline to the MOU for BYOK language (will send to Legal after you review).

-rishi

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@megabank.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Deliverables: custody/retention evidence for Mega Bank (SIG)

Samantha —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review we've attached the artifacts requested:

- retention_policy_snippet.pdf (excerpt showing default request-log retention and optional config for longer retention)
- dataflow_diagram_v3.png (anonymized, shows ephemeral stores and KV cache TTL)
- redwood_soc2_artifact_list.xlsx (index of SOC 2 artifacts and mapping to SIG control sections)
- access_matrix.csv (role-level access to production keys and custodians; redacted at user level)
- docusign_mou_draft.pdf (proposal for BYOK/BYOK contract language if you want customer-managed KMS for Hosted)

Quick clarifications inline:
- Default hosted request retention: 30 days (configurable).
- Backups/snapshots: infrastructure snapshots do not contain request payloads.
- BYOK: available via MOU above; requires legal review for contract append.

Proposed next step: 30-min walkthrough with your auditor. I'm available Wed 25th 10–12 PT or Thu 26th 14–16 PT. Let me know what works and we'll send calendar invite.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Compliance & GTM Risk
Redwood Inference
